ndba93d8da6f.s: Under Article 111, when a Money Bill is presented to the President, the President may:
o: Refer it to a joint sitting
ndba93d8da6f.x: The President may assent to or withhold assent from a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration.

n3c07f83dcfd.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
n3c07f83dcfd.x: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations; otherwise it is deemed passed by both Houses.

nb5d9070a768.s: Which of the following Bills can the President NOT return to Parliament for reconsideration?
nb5d9070a768.x: A Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration, whereas Financial Bills-I and II can be.

nae9a64f6879.s: A Financial Bill-II under Article 117(3) needs the President's recommendation at which stage?
nae9a64f6879.x: A Financial Bill-II may be introduced in either House and needs the President's recommendation only at the consideration stage.

nindian-polity-21-1.s: Under Article 79, the position of the President with respect to Parliament is that of:
o: An integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House
A member of the Rajya Sabha
A member of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-21-1.x: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the President is an integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House.

na4db53cf80e.s: If the President does not summon a joint sitting after a deadlock under Article 108, the Bill:
o: Automatically becomes law after six months
Must be referred to the Supreme Court
Is deemed passed by both Houses
na4db53cf80e.x: If the President does not summon the joint sitting, the Bill comes to an end; it does not become law automatically.

n5f6fa40573b.s: Which of the following causes all pending business before the Lok Sabha to lapse?
n5f6fa40573b.x: Only dissolution makes all pending Lok Sabha business lapse; adjournment or adjournment sine die does not make Bills lapse.

nindian-polity-61-32.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Appropriation Bill?
nindian-polity-61-32.x: Article 114 covers the Appropriation Bill; Article 112 is the Annual Financial Statement and Article 116 the vote on account.

ne5d39781d7f.s: Who audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of both the Union and the States?
ne5d39781d7f.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits all three funds of both the Union and the States.

nindian-polity-61-12.s: Which of the following is votable expenditure and not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Emoluments and office expenses of the President
Salaries and allowances of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers
nindian-polity-61-12.x: The salaries of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers are votable; the other three are charged on the CFI.

nindian-polity-79-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the salaries and pensions of judges?
o: Salaries of Supreme Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Pensions of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Salaries of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Salaries of High Court Judges are paid from the State's Consolidated Fund
nindian-polity-79-13.x: High Court judges' salaries come from the State's fund; only their pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

nindian-polity-61-17.s: The salaries and administrative expenses of the Election Commission are:
o: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Paid from the Public Account of India
Met from the Contingency Fund of India
nindian-polity-61-17.x: The Election Commission's salaries and running costs are voted, not charged.

nindian-polity-79-8.s: The Vice-President of India draws salary in the capacity of:
nindian-polity-79-8.x: The Vice-President gets no salary as Vice-President and is paid only as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

nindian-polity-79-15.s: Which Article deals with the salaries and allowances of High Court Judges?
nindian-polity-79-15.x: High Court judges' pay is under Article 221; Article 125 covers Supreme Court judges.

nindian-polity-79-30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about voted and charged expenditure?
o: The Election Commission's expenditure is votable
The salaries of the Prime Minister and Ministers are voted through Demands for Grants
The Vice-President receives a separate salary as Vice-President
The Vice-President is paid as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-79-30.x: The Vice-President is paid only as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and has no separate salary as Vice-President.

nindian-polity-38-66.s: An advance grant for part of a financial year, pending passage of the Budget, is called a:
nindian-polity-38-66.x: A vote on account is an advance grant for part of the year; the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawals for voted grants and charged expenditure.

nindian-polity-35-47.s: Inquiry committees of Parliament are examples of:
nindian-polity-35-47.x: Inquiry committees are ad hoc committees, not standing committees.

n83d07353b4c.s: How many members does the Committee of Privileges of the Rajya Sabha have?
n83d07353b4c.x: The Rajya Sabha Committee of Privileges has 10 members; the Lok Sabha committee has 15 nominated by the Speaker.

nfc060b58296.s: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 is currently before:
o: A Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
A Select Committee of the Lok Sabha
nfc060b58296.x: The Bill is before a JPC (a joint committee of both Houses), not a single-House Select Committee.

n676aa892b72.s: Departmentally Related Standing Committees were introduced in 1993 on the recommendation of the:
n676aa892b72.x: DRSCs began in 1993 with 17 committees on the recommendation of the Rules Committee and became 24 from 2004.

n31fadee81da.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary financial control?
o: Financial committees replace the budgetary process entirely
The budget exercises control before expenditure takes place
Financial committees exercise control after expenditure has taken place
Financial committees complement the budgetary process
n31fadee81da.x: Financial committees examine expenditure after the event and complement, rather than replace, the budgetary process.

n0f795b0ba9d.s: What is the quorum of a Departmentally Related Standing Committee?
n0f795b0ba9d.x: The quorum of a DRSC is 11, not 15; each DRSC has 31 members.

naf46605db41.s: Which committees scrutinise the demands for grants, referred Bills and annual reports of the ministries under them?
naf46605db41.x: DRSCs scrutinise demands for grants, referred Bills, annual reports and long-term policy of their ministries.

n1d1f88012b4.s: Since 1967, the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been an Opposition member by virtue of:
n1d1f88012b4.x: The Opposition chair of the PAC since 1967 is a convention, not a constitutional or statutory rule.

new.s: The creation of a new All-India Service under Article 312 begins with a resolution of the:
new.x: Creation of a new All-India Service starts with a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 312.

new.s: How many Private Members' Bills have become law so far?
new.x: Only 14 Private Members' Bills have become law, the last in 1970.

new.s: A Private Member's Bill can be introduced by:
o: Any MP who is not a minister
Only the Leader of the Opposition
new.x: Any MP who is not a minister may introduce a Private Member's Bill; Government Bills are introduced by ministers.

new.s: The defeat of a Government Bill in the House signals:
o: Automatic dissolution of the Lok Sabha
Reference of the Bill to a joint sitting
Loss of confidence in the government
new.x: Defeat of a Government Bill signals loss of confidence; defeat of a Private Member's Bill has no bearing on the government.

new.s: The President must give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill as a result of the:
new.x: The 24th Amendment, 1971 made it obligatory for the President to assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

new.s: If a Bill returned by the President is passed again by Parliament, the President must assent. This power is a:
new.x: Returning a Bill once is a suspensive veto; if re-passed, with or without amendment, the President must assent.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the second House on an ordinary Bill:
1. It may keep the Bill pending for six months, leading to a deadlock.
2. It must return the Bill within 14 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: For an ordinary Bill the second House has no time limit; the 14-day limit applies to the Rajya Sabha on a Money Bill.

new.s: A Bill is published in the Gazette at which stage of its passage?
new.x: At the first reading the Bill is introduced, its title and objectives are read and it is published in the Gazette.

new.s: In Rojer Mathew (2019), the Money Bill question was referred to a larger bench of:
new.x: Rojer Mathew (2019) referred the Money Bill question to a larger 7-judge bench.

new.s: Under Article 110(2), a Bill is NOT a Money Bill merely because it provides for taxes imposed by:
new.x: Taxes by local bodies for local purposes, fines and licence fees do not make a Bill a Money Bill.

new.s: The Speaker's certificate on a Money Bill is endorsed when the Bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha and to the:
new.x: The certificate is endorsed when the Bill goes to the Rajya Sabha (Art. 109) and to the President (Art. 111).

new.s: Which of the following Bills may be introduced by a private member?
new.x: Only a Financial Bill-II may be introduced by a minister or a private member; Money Bills (including the Appropriation Bill) and FB-I by a minister only.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Financial Bill-I is under Article 117(1); the Money Bill is defined in Article 110, FB-II is Article 117(3) and the joint sitting is Article 108.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT required for a Financial Bill-I?
o: Introduction only in the Lok Sabha
new.x: A Financial Bill-I needs no Speaker's certificate; that is required only for a Money Bill.

new.s: A Bill affecting taxation in which States are interested needs the President's prior recommendation under:
new.x: Article 274 requires the President's prior recommendation for Bills on taxation in which States are interested.

new.s: A State Bill imposing restrictions on inter-state trade needs, before its introduction in the State Legislature, the:
new.x: A State Bill restricting inter-state trade needs the President's previous sanction before introduction.

new.s: On the Annual Financial Statement, the Rajya Sabha can:
o: Vote on the Demands for Grants
Discuss it but not vote on the Demands for Grants
new.x: The Rajya Sabha can discuss the Annual Financial Statement, but voting on Demands for Grants (Art. 113) is only in the Lok Sabha.

new.s: When all remaining demands are put to vote without discussion on the last allotted day, it is called:
new.x: The guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last day allotted.

new.s: A policy cut motion reduces a demand for grant to:
new.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 to show disapproval of the policy; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100.

new.s: Demands for Grants are provided for under which Article?
new.x: Article 113 deals with Demands for Grants; 112 is the Annual Financial Statement, 114 the Appropriation Bill and 116 the vote on account.

new.s: The first Union Budget of independent India was presented on:
new.x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.

new.s: The quorum of a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is:
new.x: The quorum of a joint sitting is one-tenth of the total membership of both Houses.

new.s: The first joint sitting of Parliament, held in 1961, was on the:
new.x: Only three joint sittings have been held: 1961 (Dowry Prohibition), 1978 (Banking Service Commission Repeal) and 2002 (POTA).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a joint sitting under Article 108?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides
Financial Bills I and II can be referred to it
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides in the Speaker's absence
Decisions are taken by a majority of members present and voting
new.x: The Vice-President / Rajya Sabha Chairman does not preside over a joint sitting; after the Speaker and Deputy Speaker comes the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman.

new.s: A Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368 must be passed in each House by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership only
Three-fourths of members present and voting
A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
new.x: A Constitutional Amendment Bill needs a special majority in each House separately: majority of total membership plus two-thirds of members present and voting.

new.s: If the two Houses disagree on a Constitutional Amendment Bill:
o: No joint sitting can be held
The President summons a joint sitting
The Bill is referred to the Supreme Court
new.x: There is no joint sitting for a Constitutional Amendment Bill; it must pass each House separately.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about a Constitutional Amendment Bill:
1. It needs the President's prior recommendation for introduction.
2. It can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: A Constitutional Amendment Bill can start in either House, by a minister or private member, and needs no prior recommendation of the President.

new.s: On prorogation of a House, which of the following lapses?
o: Pending notices, except notices for introducing Bills
All pending business of the House
Bills passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Prorogation does not end Bills; only pending notices lapse, except notices for introducing Bills.

new.s: Which of the following Bills does NOT lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
o: A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha
A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha
A Bill passed by both Houses and pending the President's assent
A Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha and pending in the Lok Sabha
new.x: A Bill passed by both Houses and pending assent survives dissolution; Bills pending in or passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapse.

new.s: Under Article 200, the Governor may reserve a State Bill for the consideration of the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: The Governor may assent, withhold, return a non-Money Bill or reserve it for the President under Article 201.

new.s: In its November 2025 advisory opinion on a Presidential Reference, the Supreme Court held that courts:
o: Cannot fix timelines for assent or declare deemed assent
Can fix timelines for assent to State Bills
Can declare deemed assent to State Bills
Can give assent on behalf of the Governor
new.x: The five-judge Bench held that courts cannot fix timelines or declare deemed assent, unlike the April 2025 Tamil Nadu Governor judgment.

new.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, renaming the State 'Keralam', was brought under Article:
new.x: Alteration of a State's name is under Article 3; the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 was passed by the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: The Andhra State Bill introduced in Parliament on 10 August 1953 received assent on:
new.x: The Andhra State Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953 and received assent on 14 September 1953.

new.s: The Annual Financial Statement is laid before both Houses of Parliament by the order of the:
new.x: The President causes the AFS to be laid before both Houses; it is presented in the Lok Sabha by the Finance Minister.

new.s: The word 'Budget' comes from the French 'bougette', meaning:
new.x: 'Bougette' is French for little bag; the Constitution itself does not use the word 'Budget'.

new.s: The Halwa ceremony in North Block marks the:
o: Start of printing of Budget documents
new.x: The Halwa ceremony marks the start of printing of Budget documents.

new.s: Voting on Demands for Grants under Article 113 takes place in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
new.x: Only the Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants; the Rajya Sabha can only discuss the Budget.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a stage of the normal budget process?
o: Scrutiny by Departmentally Related Standing Committees
new.x: Vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants are not stages of normal financial law-making.

new.s: In budget procedure, the guillotine refers to:
o: Putting all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last allotted day
new.x: On the last allotted day, the guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote without discussion.

new.s: A Policy Cut Motion reduces a demand for grant:
new.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 to show complete disapproval of the policy behind it.

new.s: Which cut motion reduces a demand by a specified amount to seek economy in expenditure?
new.x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100 to air a grievance.

new.s: Article 114(3) provides that no money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under:
new.x: No withdrawal from the CFI is allowed except under appropriation made by law; even charged expenditure needs an Appropriation Act.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Appropriation Bill:
1. It may authorise withdrawal of more than the amount in the Annual Financial Statement.
2. No amendment may alter the destination of a voted grant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: No amendment may vary the amount or destination of a voted grant, and withdrawals cannot exceed the AFS amount.

new.s: The Appropriation Bill is a:
new.x: The Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill; the Finance Bill puts the Budget's tax proposals into effect.

new.s: Sums required to satisfy a judgment, decree or arbitral award are:
o: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Paid from the Public Account of India
Met from the Contingency Fund of India
new.x: Sums for a judgment, decree or arbitral award are charged on the CFI under Article 112(3).

new.s: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India is:
o: Put to vote but not discussed
Not put to vote but can be discussed
Voted only in the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Charged expenditure is non-votable but can be discussed in both Houses.

new.s: An additional grant under Article 115 is sanctioned for:
o: An emergency whose details cannot be stated
A new service not in the Budget
new.x: An additional grant is for a new service not in the Budget; a supplementary grant is for an insufficient amount.

new.s: Before the Lok Sabha votes an excess grant, it must be approved by the:
new.x: An excess grant needs the approval of the Public Accounts Committee first.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Article 115 covers supplementary, additional and excess grants; Article 116 covers vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants.

new.s: The Contingency Fund of India is held on behalf of the President by the:
o: Finance Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs
new.x: The Contingency Fund of India is held by the Finance Secretary, DEA, not the Department of Expenditure.

new.s: The Contingency Fund of a State is provided for under Article:
new.x: Article 267(2) provides for the State Contingency Fund; 267(1) is the Contingency Fund of India.

new.s: Treasury Bills and ways and means advances raised by the Union are credited to the:
new.x: All revenues and loans, including Treasury Bills and ways and means advances, go into the Consolidated Fund of India.

new.s: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in:
new.x: The Railway Budget, separate since 1924, was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

new.s: The first Outcome Budget and the first Gender Budget Statement relate to the year:
new.x: Both the first Outcome Budget and the first Gender Budget Statement were in 2005-06.

new.s: The first combined Railway and General Budget was presented on 1 February 2017 by:
new.x: Arun Jaitley presented the first combined Budget on 1 February 2017.

new.s: How many Rajya Sabha members are associated with the Public Accounts Committee?
new.x: The PAC has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: Members of the financial committees of Parliament are elected by:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
new.x: Members are elected yearly by proportional representation by single transferable vote; ministers are ineligible.

new.s: The chairman of the Estimates Committee is invariably from the:
new.x: The Estimates Committee chairman, appointed by the Speaker, is invariably from the ruling party; the PAC chair is from the Opposition.

new.s: The Public Accounts Committee submits its reports to the:
new.x: The PAC reports to the Lok Sabha through the Speaker.

new.s: The PAC is called a 'post-mortem' check because it examines:
new.x: The PAC examines only the execution of policy, not policy itself, after the money is spent.

new.s: Which committee is described as the 'watchdog' on departmental expenditure and irregularities?
new.x: The PAC is the watchdog on expenditure; Petitions is the 'Ombudsman' and Estimates the 'continuous economy committee'.

new.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921 under the:
new.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.

new.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the:
new.x: COPU came in 1964 on the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation.

new.s: The Estimates Committee in its present form (1950) owes its origin to the recommendation of:
new.x: The Estimates Committee took its present form in 1950 on John Mathai's recommendation.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: DRSCs began in 1993; the PAC dates from 1921, the Estimates Committee from 1950 and COPU from 1964.

new.s: Of the 24 Departmentally Related Standing Committees, how many function under the Lok Sabha?
new.x: There are 24 DRSCs: 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines:
o: The use of delegated rule-making powers
new.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks the use of delegated rule-making powers.

new.s: Which committee tracks the assurances given by ministers until they are implemented?
new.x: The Committee on Government Assurances tracks ministers' assurances till implemented.

new.s: Which committee allots time for government and other business in the Lok Sabha?
new.x: The Business Advisory Committee, chaired by the Speaker, allots time for government and other business.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs:
1. Ministers cannot serve on it.
2. It examines welfare programmes for SCs and STs in Union ministries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: ministers cannot serve on the committee, and it examines SC/ST welfare programmes in Union ministries and bodies.

new.s: How many Lok Sabha members are on the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs?
new.x: The committee has 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: A Joint Parliamentary Committee investigated the Bofors issue in:
new.x: The Bofors JPC was in 1987; Harshad Mehta 1992, Ketan Parekh 2001 and 2G spectrum 2011.

new.s: The JPC on the 2G spectrum issue was constituted in:
new.x: The 2G spectrum JPC was in 2011, the last of the listed scam JPCs.
